mod.overview: Renegades Duel (HaVoC, July 2002) puts one-on-one duel rules on top of an unchanged Renegades Classic 1.1c rule set; its items are identical to Classic. Duel maps switch the server to one of two systems: RenDuel.cs, where any two players challenge each other from the Tab menu and fight in one of 12 arenas, or duelmatch.cs, a single-elimination tournament run one duel at a time. Classes, stations and team play are bypassed: every duelist spawns as a light-armor Sniper with a loadout they choose, and only their current opponent can hurt them.
notes: Loading: each duel map ends with exec(RenDuel) or exec(duelmatch). On every mission load Server::loadMission calls DuelMOD::restoreServerDefaults, which execs resetduel.cs, admin, player, objectives, observer and game, so a following non-duel map gets normal Renegades rules back. resetduel.cs restores the stock Lightning::damageTarget and the Classic MineAmmo handler; its restores of the Classic Grenade and Beacon handlers were added by the port (its own comment says the 2002 archive never restored those two).

Challenge duels (RenDuel.cs): select a player in the Tab menu and pick 'Request Duel'. They have 30 seconds to accept (requesting them back, or 'acceptduel' from the list of pending challenges, starts it). You cannot duel yourself, someone already in a duel, or someone who has turned duels off with the Miscellany menu's 'Disable Duels'. Requests are refused until the match has started.

Arenas: DuelInit picks a random free spot from MissionGroup/Duel1 to Duel12; each group's first two objects are the two spawn markers. If no spot is free after 60 random tries the duel is cancelled. Both duelists are put on the same team, numbered after the spot (spots 1-8 use teams 0-7, spots 9-12 use teams 0-3).

Start sequence: both players are locked in an orbiting pregame camera for a 7-second countdown ('READY!', then a seconds count), then 'FIGHT!'. Damage is enabled 1.5 s ($DuelHurtDelay) after FIGHT, and both players' damage is reset to 0 at the start.

Damage rule: Player::onDamage and Lightning::damageTarget ignore any hit unless both shooter and target are in a duel, damage is enabled, and the shooter's opponent is the target (self-damage is allowed). Everything else, including other duelists and stray fire, does nothing. Knockback, shields and $DamageScale still apply; Laser head hits do 30% extra.

Loadout: duelists always spawn in larmor (lfemale for female players) with 3 weapons and 1 pack. Weapons can be chosen from Chaingun, Sniper Rifle, Disc Launcher, Grenade Launcher, Laser Rifle, Plasma Gun, ELF Gun (EnergyRifle), Blaster and Hyper Blaster; the default is Disc Launcher, Sniper Rifle, Grenade Launcher. Packs are Energy, Repair, Shield or Ammo Pack (default Energy). Ammo is set to the armor's $ItemMax, plus $AmmoPackMax with the Ammo Pack. Everyone also gets 3 mines, 5 grenades, 1 Repair Kit and 3 beacons.

Duel items: Grenade throws a plain Handgrenade (throw force 9, not Classic's 15). Mine throws an antipersonelMine; up to three per player are tracked and destroyed when the duel ends. Beacon throws a Speed Booster mine.

Ending: a death ends the duel. The winner gets +1 score and a win-streak counter; streaks over 1 are shown with extra exclamation marks at 4, 8 and 13. If neither player has an energy weapon, a check 30 s after FIGHT (then every 15 s) declares a draw once both are out of ammo. Leaving the server aborts the duel. After 4 s ($DuelDelayTime) both return to observer mode and the arena is freed.

Records (RenDuel.cs): with more than 4 clients on the server, the fastest win ever and the longest win streak are announced and exported to config\RDuelRecord.cs, which is loaded again at startup. A per-map best time is also kept.

No class mechanics: Player::onCollision just returns (no corpse looting or touch effects), Player::leaveMissionArea does nothing in RenDuel.cs, and new players join as observers with 'Press tab and select a player to duel!!!'. Observers can follow a duelist and are told whenever that duelist lands a hit.

Tournament (duelmatch.cs): after the match starts every player is 'not ready' and readies up by pressing fire while observing; the game names whoever is holding things up. Once everyone is ready, InitPartners pairs the remaining players at random and the tournament begins 10 s later. Players can opt out ($DuelTModeOff) and late joiners after the start are not entered.

Tournament rounds: only one duel runs at a time, always in arena Duel1, with a 9-second countdown; all other players are switched to watch one of the two duelists. The loser is eliminated ($DuelAlive false). When every pairing in a round has fought, the next round re-pairs the survivors; an odd player out waits. The final pairing is announced as a duel 'for first place'. When fewer than two survivors remain the winner is recorded and the server moves to the next mission 5 s later.
Tournament out-of-area rule: during a live duel, leaving the mission area costs 0.05 damage per second until you return or die, and such a death counts as a loss.

Port files (Modern Tribes 1.50 port, per the header of RenegadesDuel.cs, not part of the 2002 release): duelport.cs adds RenDuelPort::optAllowed, which re-checks admin rights and vote settings for every Tab-menu option code a client sends, and supplies hvcAdminMsg for duelmatch.cs. duelshapes.cs defines the map decorations (a destructible BigAssSatDD sensor, powered fire, beam and light shapes that fade in and out with power, a fast 4x4 elevator) and the Miscellany observer-mode menu (Free, Fixed, 1st Person).

Script bugs: the 'Wrong Target!' message in Player::onDamage and Lightning::damageTarget is sent to %foeId, which is never set there, so nobody sees it. The duel Beacon::onUse calls Player::decItemCount twice per use. In PlayersOutOfAmmo the opponent's ammo is checked against the first player's weapon setup, not the opponent's own. The duel MineAmmo::onUse never sets the mine's team.
